title: SAML session consistency: implicit JIT provisioning, MFA hinting, and admin-forced logout
creator: Jordan Kim
description:
Background: When customers use SSO via SAML, we currently create sessions tied to a short-lived session cookie and a server-side session record. Edge cases around Just-In-Time (JIT) provisioning, MFA expectations, and admin-initiated logout are causing inconsistencies: users can be provisioned without clear MFA hints, admin forced-logout doesn't reliably invalidate long-lived tokens in Dedicated/Private deployments, and audit logs don't always capture the causal chain (SAML assertion -> JIT user create -> MFA required -> session start).

Problem statement: We need a single, auditable model for SAML session establishment and termination that handles: implicit/JIT provisioning with an MFA expectation flag, a reproducible forced-logout flow that covers browser sessions and long-lived API keys/tokens, and deterministic re-auth behavior (when to surface MFA step-up vs silent session renewal). Current failures cause confusing UX (users prompted unexpectedly) and security gaps (tokens surviving admin logout), and make incident investigation harder because causal links are missing from logs.

Goals:
- Define and implement a session state machine for SAML flows that includes a JIT_provisioned attribute and mfa_hint attribute.
- Ensure admin-forced-logout invalidates session records and associated refresh tokens and long-lived keys across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private.
- Emit structured audit events for every state transition (SAML assertion received, JIT create, MFA required, MFA passed, session.created, session.terminated, admin.force_logout) including correlation_id.
- Surface clear UI/console indicators when a user's account was provisioned via SAML JIT and whether MFA was required at provisioning time.
- Define re-auth policies: time-based grace window for silent renewal, explicit step-up when critical admin actions are attempted, and configurable tenant-wide enforcement for MFA step-up frequency.

Proposed implementation (high level):
1) Session state machine: add fields on session records: "provision_source" (values: 'builtin', 'sso_jit', 'sso_existing'), "mfa_hint" (values: 'none', 'required', 'recommended'), "correlation_id" (string uuid), "ttl_policy" (enum referencing tenant config). Server enforces transitions: assertion -> JIT create -> mfa required -> session.start OR assertion -> existing user -> evaluate mfa_hint -> session.start.
2) JIT provisioning path: when a SAML assertion contains attributes triggering create, set provision_source='sso_jit' and mfa_hint according to IdP assertion and tenant policy. If mfa_hint='required', surface a post-provisioning step that blocks non-interactive token issuance until MFA confirmation.
3) Forced-logout: add atomic invalidation operations that mark session records as terminated and emit an audit event. For Dedicated/Private, run a distributed revocation RPC that marks tokens invalid in local caches and rotation services. Long-lived API keys associated with the user get a revocation marker; background sweep ensures batched revocation within 60s.
4) Audit logging: switch to structured JSON events with fields: timestamp, correlation_id, actor, actor_role, target_user, event_type, source (SAML assertion id if present), tenant_id, request_id, trace_id, metadata. Persist to the existing audit pipeline and increment retention for admin actions to 6 months for enterprise customers.
5) Re-auth policy: implement tenant config with three knobs: silent_renew_grace_seconds (default 300), stepup_actions (list, default ['console.critical_change','api.key.rotate']), and mfa_enforcement_interval_days (default 90). Enforce step-up by rejecting the action with a 401-like challenge that includes reason and correlation id for logging.

Non-goals: This ticket does not implement UI changes to the Console beyond adding an indicator flag and a link to the audit event. Full RBAC v2 changes and per-route token scoping will be tracked separately.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Revocation flood may strain Dedicated clusters. Mitigation: use rate-limited revocation queues and idempotent markers; fallback policy to accept short window where cached tokens may still work and log as 'revocation_pending'.
- Risk: MFA enforcement blocking CI jobs that rely on service tokens. Mitigation: allow exception via tenant-level allowlist and require explicit admin opt-in for 'mfa_required' at JIT time.

Metrics to track: number of JIT provisions per day, percent of sessions with mfa_hint='required', time-to-revoke median/95th, audit event lag, number of forced-logout incidents, and customer support tickets referencing unexpected reauth.

Deliverables: detailed design doc (Confluence link in attachments), schema migrations for session table, revocation RPC and worker, audit-event producer changes, tenant config API, console indicator, e2e integration tests, and rollout checklist.
acceptance_criteria: Session records include provision_source, mfa_hint, correlation_id, and ttl_policy and values are populated for SAML flows
Admin forced-logout marks sessions terminated and associated long-lived keys are revoked within 60s in Hosted and documented best-effort for Dedicated/Private
Structured audit events are emitted for SAML assertion handling, JIT create, MFA events, session start, and session termination with correlation_id present
Tenant-level re-auth config accepts silent_renew_grace_seconds and stepup_actions and these controls block actions with a clear challenge response
Automated tests cover JIT with mfa_hint='required' preventing non-interactive token creation until MFA confirmation
comments: 2026-03-10 - Jordan Kim: Initial ticket created after on-call incident where admin logout didn't revoke a dedicated token; added background and goals.
2026-03-11 - Aisha Patel: Draft design posted to Confluence (see attachment). Called out required schema migration and potential downtime window for session table index rebuild.
2026-03-12 - Marco Ruiz (security): Reviewed audit schema; requested inclusion of actor_role and tenant_id in events and retention note for enterprise customers.

2026-03-13 - Design review: Agreed to use correlation_id propagated from SAML assertion's InResponseTo when present, else generate server uuid. Decided revocation sweep will be best-effort in on-prem, documented in release notes.
2026-03-14 - Aisha Patel: Started implementation of revocation RPC prototype; opened PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/3842
2026-03-14 - QA: Added E2E scenarios to test matrix for SAML JIT + MFA enforcement and admin forced-logout across Hosted/Dedicated/Private
rollout_plan: Canary rollout in Hosted: enable structured audit and session fields for 10% of tenants for 48 hours, monitor metrics and revoke latency. Then enable revocation RPC in Dedicated staging, run sweep tests. For Private, ship migration and revocation worker with opt-in flag; coordinate with SE for customer rollouts.
testing_notes: Unit tests for state transitions, integration tests that simulate SAML assertions with and without create attributes, e2e for admin forced-logout confirming token rejection, load test for revocation worker at 10k revocations/min to validate queue behavior.
notes: Follow-up tickets expected: UI/Console expansion for session provenance view, RBAC v2 integration for more granular step-up rules, and migration audit to track sessions created before the schema change. Coordinate with legal for retention changes.
